PART I
Item 1. Business
Exemplar Industries, Inc. (the “company”) designs and sells industrial sensors, monitoring software and maintenance services to manufacturers in North America, Europe and Asia. The company was incorporated in Delaware in 1987 and is headquartered in Springfield.
Our strategy is to combine connected hardware with software that helps customers predict equipment failures. We sell through a direct sales force and through distributors, and we report our results in two segments: Sensors and Software & Services.
2
Exemplar Industries 2024 Form 10-K
Item 1A. Risk Factors
Our business faces many risks. The risks described below are not the only ones we face, and additional risks that we do not currently consider material could also affect our business, financial condition and results of operations in future periods.
Failure to execute our artiﬁcial intelligence strategy could harm our results. We are investing in machine learning models that analyze sensor data, and these investments may not produce the tech­nology improvements, the customer adoption or the cost savings that we expect. Competitors with larger research budgets may develop comparable features sooner, and customers may be reluctant to rely on automated recommendations for safety-critical equipment. If our models make errors, we could face warranty claims, reputational harm and regulatory scrutiny in several jurisdictions.
•We may not realize the expected benefits of our generative AI investments, which could reduce our margins and require us to record impairment charges.
•Regulation of AI systems in the European Union and the United States is changing quickly and could increase our compliance costs or limit some product features.
3
Exemplar Industries 2024 Form 10-K
Our operations depend on suppliers of semiconductors, printed circuit boards and specialty plastics. A disruption at a single supplier could delay shipments for several quarters, and price increases from suppliers could reduce our gross margin if we are unable to pass them on to customers through our contracts and price lists. We maintain safety stock for critical parts, but these measures may not be sufficient in a prolonged shortage affecting the whole industry.
We sell in more than forty countries and are exposed to changes in foreign exchange rates, tariffs, export controls and local laws. A stronger U.S. dollar reduces the reported value of our international revenue. Trade disputes could increase the cost of components that we import, and sanctions could prevent us from serving some customers. We hedge a portion of our currency exposure, but our hedges do not cover all of it and may not be effective in volatile markets.
Cyberattacks on our systems or on the connected devices of our customers could disrupt operations, expose confidential data and lead to litigation. Our software collects equipment data from customer sites, and a breach could damage trust in our platform. We invest in security controls and employee training, but attackers continue to develop new methods, and we may not detect an intrusion quickly enough to prevent harm to customers or to the company.
4
Exemplar Industries 2024 Form 10-K
We depend on attracting and keeping skilled engineers, data scientists and sales staff. Competition for these employees is intense, especially in software and data roles, and the loss of key people could slow product development. Changes in immigration policy could also make it harder to hire qualified candidates from other countries, and rising wages could increase our operating expenses faster than revenue.
Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
In 2024 we launched a company-wide productivity program built on generative AI tools for customer support, software development and finance operations. We expect the program to deliver $150 million in annual run-rate cost savings by the end of 2025, and we plan to reduce support headcount by about 10 percent through attrition over the same period.
Revenue grew 12 percent in 2024, driven by software subscriptions. Operating margin improved by 1.5 points, reflecting higher software mix and lower freight costs.
